core_obligations: Record the setting (proof lines 11564-11575): under the assumed flatness QCoh(O) is a weak Serre subcategory, so the full subcategory D_QCoh(O) of D(O) consisting of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology makes sense.

One direction (proof lines 11577-11593): for M in QC(O) and any U -> V, compute H^i(M)(U) = H^i(R Gamma(U, M)) = H^i(R Gamma(V, M) tensor^L_{O(V)} O(U)) = H^i(R Gamma(V, M)) tensor_{O(V)} O(U) = H^i(M)(V) tensor_{O(V)} O(U), using flatness for the third equality and exactness of sections in the chaotic topology for the first and last; the module-level criterion then makes H^i(M) quasi-coherent for all i.

Converse (proof lines 11595-11605): if M lies in D_QCoh(O), the module-level criterion makes H^i(M)(U) = H^i(M)(V) tensor_{O(V)} O(U) for all U -> V, so flatness and the same computation show that R Gamma(V, M) tensor^L_{O(V)} O(U) -> R Gamma(U, M) is an isomorphism in D(O(U)), which is precisely the condition defining QC(O); hence QC(O) equals D_QCoh(O).
proof_roadmap: Note that D_QCoh(O) is defined, quasi-coherent modules being a weak Serre subcategory under the flatness assumption.
For M in QC(O), compute H^i(M)(U) by pull-push along U -> V and use the module-level criterion to conclude quasi-coherence of the cohomology sheaves.
Conversely, for M with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves, the same criterion turns the cartesianity identity into an isomorphism, so M lies in QC(O).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the quasi-coherent objects of the derived category with the complexes whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent, for a category with chaotic topology whose restriction maps are flat (statement lines 11552-11561). The proof (proof lines 11563-11605) runs the same computation in both directions: for M in QC(O) it evaluates H^i(M)(U) as H^i(R Gamma(V,M)) tensor_{O(V)} O(U) using flatness and the exactness of sections in the chaotic topology, hence the cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent; conversely quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves satisfy the module-level criterion, which turns the cartesianity identity into an isomorphism. H2: one computation applied twice, written out.
